fullPassage:
Hey there! Let me introduce you to a fascinating piece of Korean history. Back on February 9, 1795, something remarkable happened in front of Changdeokgung Palace, where King Jeongjo lived. There was quite a crowd gathered there to witness a very special procession that's still talked about in Korea today.
Now, imagine this: more than 2,000 soldiers, hundreds of horse riders, and lots of important officials, all marching alongside the king and his mother with 50 musicians playing traditional instruments. When they crossed a bridge made of 36 boats on the Hangang River, you can imagine how that turned heads! That must have been something ordinary people rarely saw. Talk about a big event!
This was not just about putting on a show. No, it was serious business. Lasting four days and covering 68 kilometers, the procession moved alongside the king and his mother as they made a round trip to Hwaseong Haenggung.
Why did all of this happen? The first thing King Jeongjo had in mind was to show respect to his family. It happened around his mother's sixtieth birthday. Back in the Joseon Dynasty, just like today, turning 60 years old had a special meaning. And his father's tomb was near Hwaseong Haenggung. He was planning to hold a memorial service to honor his late father. By combining the two events, he was telling everyone how much family meant to him.
But wait. There's more. King Jeongjo was also making a statement about the Joseon Dynasty's strength. He dressed up like a military leader, wearing armor and sitting on a horse with his soldiers marching in perfect order. It was a way of saying, "We're ready to protect our land." He was really serious about making the Joseon Dynasty a powerful and successful kingdom.
Now, here's the twist: the procession also had something to do with Hwaseong Fortress, which was being built. In King Jeongjo's mind were big plans for Hwaseong. He wanted it to be a self-sufficient city with a strong military, farming, and trade as he hoped to make it the new capital, away from all the political chaos in Hanyang. So King Jeongjo gathered the best talents, such as Jeong Yakyong, and let them bring together the finest architectural techniques of his time from both the East and the West to build Hwaseong Fortress.
There's more to King Jeongjo's story. He treated his people well during the construction of the fortress. They received fair wages and breaks during bad weather and were even paid when they were sick, something that was unheard of at that time. Back then, ordinary people were typically required to work on public projects without getting paid. Once people got wind of King Jeongjo's plan, workers from all over the country came together in a rush. So, in under three years was the project finished, though it was initially thought to take about 10 years. Impressive, right?
Let's go back to the procession. The procession wasn't just some fancy show for ordinary people. It was actually a way for them to get up close and personal with the king. King Jeongjo set up a chance during the procession for common people to meet him and to share their concerns. This was a big deal, especially for those who couldn't read or write. They didn't have any other way to tell the king what was on their minds, so this was a direct line to him.
And here's the cherry on top: through the procession, King Jeongjo made government more accessible. During that time, the government used to hold exams to hire officials every three years. So, there weren't many chances available. He added special exams during the procession, giving more people a shot at joining the government. This move was innovative back then and made the government more diverse.
And guess what? King Jeongjo didn't forget a single detail. He made sure everything was documented properly by creating records for the procession and the construction of Hwaseong Fortress. These construction records were especially a lifesaver when the fortress was damaged during wartime. They were even part of why UNESCO recognized Hwaseong Fortress as a World Heritage Site.
At first, the people at UNESCO were a bit unsure about recognizing Hwaseong Fortress as the real deal. They weren't totally convinced it was authentic. But after checking out translated documents and comparing them with the restored fortress, they finally came around and agreed that the fortress had actually been restored just the way it was meant to be.
And among the records of the procession, there are these amazing paintings. One painting, Hwaneo Haengryeoldo, doesn't just feature the king's crew, but it also shows ordinary people watching along the road. It's a different take from the usual art of that time, which only focused on important figures.
So being kind to the people was a big deal for kings of the Joseon Dynasty. King Jeongjo's 1795 procession and Hwaseong Fortress stand as proof of that spirit. Hwaseong is more than just a fortress; it symbolizes a king who cared for his people. And this is a significant part of Korean cultural heritage.

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
...more than 2,000 soldiers, hundreds of horse riders, and lots of important officials, all ______ alongside the king and his mother with 50 musicians playing traditional instruments.

det.ref:
[원문] ...all marching alongside the king and his mother with 50 musicians playing traditional instruments.
[해석] ...모든 이들이 50명의 전통 악기 연주자들과 함께 왕과 그의 어머니 옆에서 행진하고 있었다. [문장 05 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ① marching — 독립분사구문(주어 생략)으로, 동시 상황(행진하는 모습)을 묘사하는 현재분사가 적절하다. 「명사 + 현재분사」 구조로 부대상황 표현.
wrongs: ① marching ✅ — 현재분사, 동시 진행 동작
② to march ❌ — to부정사는 목적/의도, 동시 상황 묘사 부적절
③ march ❌ — 동사원형은 분사구문에 쓸 수 없음
④ marched ❌ — 과거형 동사, 구문상 불가
⑤ having marched ❌ — 완료분사는 선행 동작에 사용, 동시 상황 아님
det.tip:
💡 분사구문 (현재분사)
• 동시 상황: S + V ~, 현재분사 ~
• all marching = and they were all marching

⚠️ 함정
• to부정사와 분사 구분: 목적·의도 vs 동시동작

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
When they crossed a bridge ______ of 36 boats on the Hangang River, you can imagine how that turned heads!

det.ref:
[원문] When they crossed a bridge made of 36 boats on the Hangang River
[해석] 그들이 한강 위 36척의 배로 만든 다리를 건넜을 때 [문장 06 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ② made — 과거분사 made가 bridge를 수식. 다리가 "만들어진" 것이므로 수동 의미의 과거분사가 적절. 「명사 + p.p.」 = 수동적 수식.
wrongs: ① making ❌ — 현재분사는 능동/진행, 다리가 스스로 만드는 것 아님
② made ✅ — 과거분사, 수동 의미 (만들어진 다리)
③ to make ❌ — to부정사는 목적/예정, 여기서는 이미 만들어진 상태
④ having made ❌ — 완료분사, 주어의 능동 동작에 사용
⑤ was made ❌ — 동사(was made)가 되어 하나의 문장에 두 동사 불가
det.tip:
💡 분사의 수동/능동
• p.p. + 명사 / 명사 + p.p.: 수동 (만들어진)
• V-ing + 명사 / 명사 + V-ing: 능동 (만드는)

⚠️ 함정
• was made를 넣으면 동사 2개 → 문법 오류

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 밑줄 친 부분과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
That must have been something ordinary people rarely saw.

det.ref:
[원문] That must have been something ordinary people rarely saw.
[해석] 그것은 보통 사람들이 좀처럼 보기 힘든 것이었음에 틀림없다. [문장 07 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ① seldom — rarely = seldom = 좀처럼 ~않는, 거의 ~않는. 부정 의미의 빈도부사.
wrongs: ① seldom ✅ — rarely와 동의어 (거의 ~않는)
② often ❌ — 자주 (반의어)
③ usually ❌ — 보통, 대개 (반의어에 가까움)
④ frequently ❌ — 빈번하게 (반의어)
⑤ always ❌ — 항상 (반의어)
det.tip:
💡 빈도부사 순서
• always > usually > often > sometimes > seldom/rarely > never

⚠️ rarely = seldom = hardly ever (부정 의미)

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
______ four days and covering 68 kilometers, the procession moved alongside the king and his mother as they made a round trip to Hwaseong Haenggung.

det.ref:
[원문] Lasting four days and covering 68 kilometers, the procession moved...
[해석] 4일간 지속되고 68킬로미터를 이동하며, 행렬은 왕과 어머니와 함께 화성행궁까지 왕복했다. [문장 11 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ① Lasting — 분사구문(현재분사). 주절의 주어 the procession과 일치하며, 부대상황(기간+거리)을 설명. last는 자동사이므로 능동(현재분사).
wrongs: ① Lasting ✅ — 현재분사 분사구문, 동시/부대상황
② Lasted ❌ — 과거형 동사, 분사구문 아님. 접속사 없이 동사 2개 불가
③ To last ❌ — to부정사는 목적/의도, 여기서는 부대상황
④ It lasted ❌ — 절(S+V), 접속사 없이 주절과 연결 불가
⑤ Having been lasted ❌ — last는 자동사, 수동태 불가
det.tip:
💡 분사구문
• V-ing ~, S + V: 동시/부대상황/이유
• 분사의 의미상 주어 = 주절 주어

⚠️ 함정
• last는 자동사 → 수동태 불가 (lasted ≠ was lasted)

questions.passage: The procession wasn't just some fancy show for ordinary people. ( ___ ), it was actually a way for them to get up close and personal with the king.
questions.stem: 위 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 연결사를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 6자, R로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] The procession wasn't just some fancy show for ordinary people. It was actually a way for them to get up close and personal with the king.
[해석] 행렬은 보통 사람들을 위한 단순한 화려한 쇼가 아니었다. 오히려 그것은 그들이 왕과 가까이 만날 수 있는 방법이었다. [문장 37-38 참고]
det.correct: 정답: Rather — "단순한 쇼가 아니었다"에 이어 "오히려 ~한 방법이었다"로 앞 내용을 정정/보완하는 Rather가 적절.
det.tip:
💡 연결사 Rather
• not A. Rather, B: A가 아니라, 오히려 B
• = Instead / On the contrary

⚠️ However(역접)와 구분: However는 반대 내용, Rather는 정정/대체

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
The first thing King Jeongjo had in mind was ______ respect to his family.

det.ref:
[원문] The first thing King Jeongjo had in mind was to show respect to his family.
[해석] 정조가 마음에 품은 첫 번째 것은 가족에게 존경을 표하는 것이었다. [문장 13 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ③ to show — 주어 The first thing... was 뒤의 보어로 to부정사가 적절. 「주어(thing) + be동사 + to-V」 구조.
wrongs: ① showing ❌ — 동명사도 문법적으로 가능하나 원문은 to show
② shown ❌ — 과거분사, 보어 자리에 부적절
③ to show ✅ — to부정사 보어, the thing was to ~
④ show ❌ — 동사원형, be동사 뒤 보어 불가
⑤ having shown ❌ — 완료분사, 보어 부적절
det.tip:
💡 to부정사 보어
• S + be + to-V: ~하는 것이다
• The plan was to build / The goal is to achieve

⚠️ 동명사(showing)도 가능하나 원문 기준 to-V 출제

questions.stem:
다음 문장에서 어법상 옳은 것을 고르시오.
In King Jeongjo's mind ______ big plans for Hwaseong.

det.ref:
[원문] In King Jeongjo's mind were big plans for Hwaseong.
[해석] 정조의 마음속에는 화성에 대한 큰 계획들이 있었다. [문장 26 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ① were — 장소 부사구(In King Jeongjo's mind)가 문두에 나와 주어-동사 도치. 진짜 주어는 복수 명사 big plans이므로 were.
wrongs: ① were ✅ — 도치 구문, 주어 big plans(복수) → were
② was ❌ — 주어가 big plans(복수)이므로 단수 was 불가
③ had ❌ — had plans는 "계획을 가졌다"인데, 도치구문에서는 be동사/자동사가 적절
④ have been ❌ — 현재완료, 문맥상 과거 시제 필요
⑤ being ❌ — 분사, 동사 자리에 부적절
det.tip:
💡 장소 부사구 도치
• In the room were two chairs. (← Two chairs were in the room.)
• 부사구 + 동사 + 주어(S) 어순

⚠️ 함정: mind를 주어로 착각 → was 선택 오류
• 실제 주어는 big plans(복수)!

questions.passage: By combining the two events, he was telling everyone how much family ( ______ ) to him.
questions.stem: 위 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 5자, m으로 시작)

det.ref:
[원문] By combining the two events, he was telling everyone how much family meant to him.
[해석] 두 행사를 결합함으로써, 그는 모든 사람에게 가족이 자신에게 얼마나 소중한지를 말하고 있었다. [문장 18 참고]
det.correct: 정답: meant — 「mean to + 사람」 = ~에게 의미가 있다, 소중하다. how much family meant to him: 가족이 그에게 얼마나 소중했는지.
det.tip:
💡 mean의 다양한 뜻
• mean + to-V: ~할 작정이다
• mean + O: ~을 의미하다
• mean to + 사람: ~에게 소중하다

⚠️ meant는 mean의 과거형 (mean-meant-meant)

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
He dressed up like a military leader, ______ armor and sitting on a horse with his soldiers marching in perfect order.

det.ref:
[원문] He dressed up like a military leader, wearing armor and sitting on a horse with his soldiers marching in perfect order.
[해석] 그는 갑옷을 입고 말 위에 앉아 군사 지도자처럼 차려입었다. [문장 22 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ④ wearing — 분사구문(현재분사). 주어 He가 직접 갑옷을 "입는" 능동 동작이므로 현재분사 wearing이 적절. 「, V-ing」 = 동시 상황.
wrongs: ① to wear ❌ — to부정사는 목적·의도, 동시동작 묘사 부적절
② worn ❌ — 과거분사는 수동, He가 입히는 것 아님
③ being worn ❌ — 수동진행, 갑옷이 입혀지고 있는 뜻
④ wearing ✅ — 현재분사, 능동·동시 상황
⑤ wears ❌ — 현재시제 동사, 접속사 없이 동사 2개 불가
det.tip:
💡 분사구문 + and
• , wearing A and sitting B = 두 동시 동작
• 주어가 직접 하는 동작 → 현재분사(V-ing)

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 가장 적절한 것은?
The procession also had something to do with Hwaseong Fortress, ①which ②was being built at the time, and King Jeongjo wanted ③it to be ④a self-sufficient city ⑤where people could thrive.

det.ref:
[원문] the procession also had something to do with Hwaseong Fortress, which was being built.
[해석] 행렬은 또한 건설 중이던 화성과도 관련이 있었다. [문장 25, 27 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ⑤ where — 장소 선행사(city) 뒤에 관계부사 where가 적절. 모든 밑줄 부분이 어법상 옳으며, ⑤도 올바르다. ★ 모두 옳은 문장에서 "가장 적절한 것"을 고르는 유형.
wrongs: ① which ✅ — 계속적 용법 관계대명사, 선행사 Hwaseong Fortress
② was being built ✅ — 과거 진행 수동태, 건설 중이던
③ it ✅ — 가목적어 아닌 대명사, wanted it to be 구조
④ a self-sufficient ✅ — 형용사+명사, 관사 사용 적절
⑤ where ✅ — 장소 관계부사, city를 수식
det.tip:
💡 관계대명사 vs 관계부사
• which: 뒤에 불완전한 절 (주어/목적어 빠짐)
• where: 뒤에 완전한 절 (= in which)

⚠️ 모두 맞는 선지 → 소거법 활용

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
He wanted it ______ a self-sufficient city with a strong military, farming, and trade.

det.ref:
[원문] He wanted it to be a self-sufficient city with a strong military, farming, and trade
[해석] 그는 그것이 강력한 군사력, 농업, 그리고 무역을 갖춘 자급자족 도시가 되기를 원했다. [문장 27 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ③ to be — 「want + 목적어 + to-V」 구문. 목적격보어로 to부정사가 필수.
wrongs: ① be ❌ — 동사원형, want는 사역동사 아님 → to 필요
② being ❌ — 동명사/분사, want+O+V-ing 구조 없음
③ to be ✅ — want+O+to-V 구문
④ was ❌ — 과거 동사, 보어 자리 부적절
⑤ been ❌ — p.p., 구문상 불가
det.tip:
💡 want + O + to-V
• I want you to come. (O)
• I want you come. (X) — 사역동사 아님!

⚠️ make/let/have + O + V원형 (사역)
vs want/expect/allow + O + to-V (비사역)

questions.stem:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
So King Jeongjo gathered the best talents, such as Jeong Yakyong, and let them ______ together the finest architectural techniques.

det.ref:
[원문] ...and let them bring together the finest architectural techniques of his time from both the East and the West
[해석] 그리하여 정조는 정약용과 같은 최고의 인재를 모았고, 동서양의 가장 뛰어난 건축 기술을 결합하게 했다. [문장 28 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ④ bring — 사역동사 let + 목적어 + 동사원형. let them bring = 그들이 ~하게 하다.
wrongs: ① to bring ❌ — let은 사역동사, to부정사 X
② bringing ❌ — 현재분사/동명사, let+O+V-ing 불가
③ brought ❌ — 과거분사, let+O+p.p. 불가
④ bring ✅ — 사역동사 let + O + V원형
⑤ to bringing ❌ — 구문상 불가능
det.tip:
💡 사역동사 let
• let + O + 동사원형: ~하게 하다 (허락)
• make + O + 동사원형: ~하게 시키다 (강제)
• have + O + 동사원형: ~하게 하다 (지시)

⚠️ 수동태 전환: be made to V (to 부활!) / let은 수동태 거의 안 씀

questions.stem:

• 너무 좁거나 넓은 선지 배제

ch: ① 조선 시대의 군사 훈련 방법
② 정조의 1795년 행차와 그 다층적 의미

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] ...though it was initially thought to take about 10 years.
[해석] 처음에는 약 10년이 걸릴 것으로 생각되었다. [문장 34 참고]
det.correct: 정답: ③ — 본문에 따르면 약 "10년"이 걸릴 것으로 예상되었으나, ③은 "5년"이라고 했으므로 내용 불일치.
wrongs: ① ✅ 일치 — 문장 05: more than 2,000 soldiers
② ✅ 일치 — 문장 11: four days, 68 kilometers
③ ❌ 불일치 — 약 10년 예상(원문) ≠ 5년(선지)
④ ✅ 일치 — 문장 39: for common people to meet him
⑤ ✅ 일치 — 문장 31: even paid when they were sick
det.tip:
💡 내용일치 문제
• 숫자, 기간, 이름 등 세부사항 주의
• 선지의 숫자가 본문과 다른지 꼭 확인!

ch: ③ 화성은 원래 약 5년 만에 완공될 예정이었다.
④ 정조는 행렬 중 백성들이 직접 왕을 만날 기회를 마련했다.
⑤ 화성 건설 노동자들은 아플 때도 임금을 받았다.

questions.stem:
다음 요약문의 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 8자, h로 시작)
King Jeongjo's 1795 procession was not just a grand show but a meaningful event demonstrating his respect for family, military power, and care for ordinary people — reflecting the Korean cultural ( ______ ) of the Joseon Dynasty.

det.ref:
[원문] And this is a significant part of Korean cultural heritage.
[해석] 이것은 한국 문화유산의 중요한 부분이다. [문장 61 참고]
det.correct: 정답: heritage — 본문 마지막 문장에서 Korean cultural heritage(한국 문화유산)로 언급.
det.tip:
💡 heritage
• cultural heritage: 문화유산
• World Heritage Site: 세계문화유산
• heritage = 유산, 전통

questions.stem: 윗글을 읽고 추론할 수 없는 것은?

det.ref:
[원문] 전체 지문 참고
[해석] 정조는 화성을 새 수도로 만들기를 "희망"했다고만 언급, 실제 공식 지정 여부는 본문에 없다.
det.correct: 정답: ⑤ — 본문은 "he hoped to make it the new capital"(새 수도로 만들기를 희망했다)고만 하며, 실제 공식 지정되었다는 내용은 없다.
wrongs: ① ✅ 추론 가능 — 어머니 생일 축하, 아버지 제사 → 효심
② ✅ 추론 가능 — 문장 28: from both the East and the West
③ ✅ 추론 가능 — 문장 45: special exams, more people a shot
④ ✅ 추론 가능 — 문장 56: also shows ordinary people
⑤ ❌ 추론 불가 — hoped to make it the new capital ≠ 공식 지정
det.tip:
💡 추론 불가 문제
• 본문에 "희망/계획"만 있는 것 ≠ 실제 실현
• hoped to = ~하기를 희망했다 (실현 여부 불명)

ch: ② 화성 건설에 동서양의 건축 기술이 활용되었다.
③ 행렬 중 특별 시험은 관직 진출 기회를 늘렸다.
④ 화노행렬도에는 왕뿐만 아니라 백성도 그려져 있다.
⑤ 화성은 정조 생전에 새 수도로 공식 지정되었다.

questions.stem:
다음 주제문의 빈칸에 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영문 10자, s로 시작)
Hwaseong is more than just a fortress; it ( ______ ) a king who cared for his people.

det.ref:
[원문] Hwaseong is more than just a fortress; it symbolizes a king who cared for his people.
[해석] 화성은 단순한 성곽 그 이상이다; 그것은 백성을 아낀 왕을 상징한다. [문장 60 참고]
det.correct: 정답: symbolizes — 화성은 단순한 성곽이 아니라 백성을 아끼는 왕을 상징(symbolize)한다.
det.tip:
💡 symbolize
• = represent, stand for
• 상징하다
• symbol (n.) → symbolize (v.) → symbolic (adj.)
